title: Help The Homeless in New York City with Backpacks For The Street
description: Backpacks For The Street is a boots on the ground nonprofit providing life-saving assistance to New Yorkers struggling with homelessness, 365 days a year through its well-know backpacks program, along with assistance with food, clothing and other necessitates, as well as help with employment, health care, and housing, among other essential services to those in need, including immigrants and asylum seekers, the LGBTQ and BIPOC communities. There are multiple volunteer opportunities including helping with packing and assembling backpacks, clothes, and other amazing programs, as well as our street outreach to provide food and backpacks to the unhoused communities. Since 2018, Backpacks For The Street has assisted more than 152,000 New Yorkers in need (as of July 2025). A big part of our mission is going out into the community and helping people where they are rather than wait for them to come to us. It's that human interaction and treating people with difficult circumstances with the same dignity, compassion and respect that we all want to be treated with that is at the core of our work. Homeless does not mean hopeless. We strongly encourage interested volunteers to check out our Instagram page, @backpacksforthestret , or Facebook page , as it gives a great overview of our work and the people we help. For people looking to help with giving out backpacks, we operate 365 days a year in all the boroughs rotating days throughout the week. Shifts run about an hour and a half. For people looking to help with packing and assembling, we pack backpacks a couple times a week at our warehouse in Jamaica, Queens, shifts run a few hours. Backpacks For The Street is an inclusive organization, providing a safe space for its volunteers and clients, regardless of age, gender, gender identity, religion, politics, sexual orientation, ethnicity, race, disability or musical tastes. To register as a volunteer go to: https://bfts.org/volunteer . For more information, you can check out our website at https://bfts.org . If you have any other questions, please contact us at: volunteer@bfts.org

For decades, ATW has remained committed to running this award-winning programs even while arts funding has dwindled. We have done this by relying on people-power. In our impressive 35th year, we are looking for professional, mature, and fully vaccinated adults to share their compassion by mentoring these precious children during holiday season. This training session will provide you with tools to tap into your creative potential and help you to better articulate your thoughts and ideas. You will gain an understanding of the ideas and concepts behind BNW and will learn the skills required to work with the children in our program. Bilingual Spanish speakers are highly encouraged to join us! We are looking for support translating English to Spanish because we work with a multilingual group of children.

title: Mentors needed for Fall/Holiday Theatre Program for Homeless Children!
description: The Actors Theatre Workshop (ATW), a non-profit theater and community center, is looking for Volunteer Mentors to join its Fall/Holiday Season to mentor children in and work in a production team for its Builders of the New World’s annual year-end theater arts education program for children living in the NYC shelter system . The children’s program culminates in a Creative Class and Holiday Celebration on Wednesday, Dec.11 , where you would participate in and mentor the children in a creative class. Being displaced by homelessness does not always allow a child the opportunity to have a traditional family gathering complete with nutritious food and gifts. For decades, ATW has remained committed to running this award-winning programs even while arts funding has dwindled. We have done this by relying on people-power. In our impressive 34th year, we are looking for professional, mature, and fully vaccinated adults to share their professional skills in a production team to organize the Food, Gifts, market and support other administrative and production aspects of the program, and to share their compassion by mentoring these precious children during the Dec 11th Creative Class and Holiday Celebration. Be a part of ATW’s Builders of the New World program: Apply to be a part of our volunteer and mentorship team by filling out this short application . Attend a mandatory in-person training with our Artistic Director, Thurman E. Scott, on Tuesday, December 10th,  6:00pm - 9:30pm . This training session will provide you with tools to tap into your creative potential and help you to better articulate your thoughts and ideas. You will gain an understanding of the ideas and concepts behind BNW and will learn the skills required to work with the children in our program. Join a BNW Program production team and support on a flexible weekly basis in Production, Event Planning, Marketing, Video, Fundraising, Food/Gifts. Bilingual Spanish speakers are highly encouraged to join us! We are looking for support translating English to Spanish because we work with a multilingual group of children.

title: Volunteers are needed this Christmas season!
time_label: 12/25/254:30 PM3 hours
description: Bowery Residents’ Committee (BRC) is one of New York City’s largest and most comprehensive social service agencies, committed to supporting individuals who are experiencing homelessness or are at risk of becoming homeless. Each day, we see how deeply compassion can transform lives—and it is the generosity of volunteers like you that enables us to fulfill our mission with both heart and impact. The holiday season is our busiest time of year, and also one of the most meaningful. For many of the individuals we serve, Christmas can be a painful reminder of hardship and loss. Yet with the support of volunteers, it also becomes a moment of comfort, dignity, and genuine human connection. This year, BRC will host holiday celebrations at multiple locations across Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, and the Bronx on Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, and during the days leading up to the holiday (multiple shifts will be available between December 17 and December 25). These gatherings bring warmth, joy, and a true sense of community to those we serve—and your participation would make an especially meaningful difference. Activities can include decorating and set-up of the service and dining areas, meal service, and post-meal clean up. If you’re interested in volunteering, please note that all volunteers must complete the BRC New Volunteer Registration Form (a link will be provided once you submit your interest here) and attend a brief orientation session . The sooner you complete these steps, the more opportunities will be available to you. Shifts are filled on a first-come, first-served basis and tend to reach capacity quickly, so early registration is encouraged. By planning ahead, you’ll have the best chance of securing a role that fits your schedule and allows you to make the greatest impact. Please note: Volunteers must be at least 18 years old to participate. We are not able to accommodate large groups at this time. Important: Please disregard any reference to specific locations, days, dates, or times that may appear in this posting. Each BRC program — located in Manhattan, Queens, the Bronx, and Brooklyn — will host its own holiday celebration on different days and times, both prior to and on the holiday itself. These shifts will be made available to those who have pre-registered once scheduling opens.

description: Video Volunteers needed for Non Profit Theater/Community Center that serves homeless children in NYC. Discover how you can grow creatively as a video volunteer while serving your community at an award-winning non-profit theater.  We are building a volunteer video team with professional-level skills to edit footage of the groundbreaking work occurring at The Actors Theatre Workshop. ATW has long been on the front lines of disciplined, creative training for theater professionals and individuals committed to fulfilling their creative potential. It has also been a safe haven for thousands of at-risk and homeless youth. Our original theater and education techniques have been tremendously successful with both our professional acting students and the children we teach in our after-school Builders of the New World program. We have many years of footage from our adult acting workshops and community programs that we want to share with you and the world.  After sharing a selection of these videos online and receiving such positive feedback from every corner of the globe, we are taking steps to make more of our work accessible. Our editors often talk about the beautiful deeply moving moments they witness when a student, actor, or a child from a homeless shelter brings forth their talent and reaches for their potential. By working with this material, you will gain deeper insight into the emotional and psychological breakdown of drama, and the importance of script analysis, which are both essential to creating compelling narratives through film. Bigs & Littles NYC Mentoring is...

Founded in 1902, Bigs & Littles NYC Mentoring strives to transform the lives of children through one-to-one mentoring, while strengthening entire families in hardship.

In Bigs & Littles NYC’s keystone mentoring program, youth ages 7-19 (enrollment till age 17), are carefully matched with a Big Sister or Big Brother who serves as adviser, role model, and adult friend. Mentoring matches meet twice monthly for activities such as enjoying a show or ballgame, working together on a service project, or spending time talking and exploring NYC. Matches are supported by a dedicated Professional Program Manager to oversee and guide the match relationship, offering referrals and additional resources as needed. Our holistic approach to mentoring consists of working closely with the entire family ensuring better outcomes. We know the program works: 100% of our kids avoid pregnancy, 100% avoid arrest, 99% are promoted to the next grade, 94% graduate High School and 94% matriculate into college or a training program.

A Match is... 

  • The relationship between a Big (volunteer mentor) and a Little (mentee)
  • Bigs serve as positive role models and friends who help Littles set and accomplish goals
  • Bigs and Littles plan and participate in fun activities together which form a lasting impact for both individuals
  • Supported by a Match Coordinator (Masters level social worker or equivalent) at the agency

Bigs are ... 

  • 21 years old or older
  • Interested in mentoring a Little of the same gender, age 7-17, who lives in the five boroughs
  • Willing and able to finance match outings (low or no-cost outings are highly encouraged)

  • From all walks of life! Men, people of color, volunteers ages 50+, individuals of all faith backgrounds, and Spanish speakers highly encouraged to apply

Big and Little matches connect... 

  • Over time: Bigs and Littles each commit to the match relationship for at least one year
  • Face-to-face: twice per month for about eight total hours (usually on the weekends)
  • Over the phone: once weekly to catch up

description: Mission Statement City Relief exists to create connections for the hurting and homeless to resources and hope. About City Relief uses mobile resource centers to assist people dealing with poverty and homelessness. These outreaches happen eight times a week in different areas of New York City and New Jersey. description: Volunteer greeters take visitors through neighborhoods of The Bronx that they know well. Visitors are able to experience the ethnic sights and sounds with the greeter and can get a real taste of The Bronx and its inhabitants. Visits may include from one to six people. Greeters must enjoy meeting and talking with people from diverse cultures and backgrounds. They must be familiar with and upbeat about the neighborhoods that they want to show. Foreign language skills are a plus, especially ASL and Spanish. If you speak a foreign language, here is your chance to practice it with native speakers. You will be able to promote a friendly, inviting and accessible image of New York City.

title: Share Your New York Story in an Interview - Neighborhood Stories Project
organization_name: NYC Department of Records and Information Services
description: The Neighborhood Stories Project is a storytelling initiative by the NYC Department of Records and Information Services (DORIS) with the mission of recording the memories of New York City residents through a series of  interviews. These interviews will be preserved in perpetuity at DORIS - connecting local history with the records of City government maintained in the collections of the Municipal Archives and Library. The interviews will reflect people’s unique experiences of life in New York City and will be available for researchers, teachers, students, activists, and residents interested in discovering the history of their city from the perspective of its community members. We are looking for participants to sit for interviews for the Neighborhood Stories Project. Participants in the project are interviewed by a trained volunteer, who will ask them questions about their lives and communities in New York City. Once recorded, the interview is preserved in perpetuity at the Municipal Archives with the goal of documenting the personal histories of local residents and changes in their communities from a personal perspective. Participants should have access to a phone (including landline), computer, or the internet. Participants should also be willing to share their stories and experiences. Volunteers can also assist the project in recruiting other participants in their families and communities by spreading the word about the Neighborhood Stories project and sharing informational materials (which can be provided). About the Interview: Interviews last roughly an hour; The interview is conducted on the platform Zoom. However, you do not need to have an account or a computer to sit for this interview. If you don’t have access to a computer or the internet, you will be able to call in from your phone (including a landline) to join the interview. Before your interview, you will be required to sign a release form, so that the recording can be preserved in the Archives; The interview will cover topics related to your personal history, specifically your experiences living in your Neighborhood. While you do not need to have lived in a New York City neighborhood for a given duration of time, you do need to be a present or past resident of New York City. If you are interested in participating in this project, please fill out this application form: https://forms.office.com/g/SASt5rm4dh After you have submitted your responses, you will be matched with a volunteer and given a time for your interview. If you have any questions, please email stories@records.nyc.gov .

description: About the team Building on its Charter mandate, the Mayor’s Office of Immigrant Affairs (MOIA) promotes the well-being of immigrant communities by recommending policies and programs that facilitate the successful integration of immigrant New Yorkers into the civic, economic, and cultural life of the City. We Speak NYC is the city’s free English Language Learning program, created and managed by MOIA. We provide civic-focused instruction through videos, web and print materials, teacher professional development, and free community classes in all five boroughs. About the opportunity This program provides in-person English classes for new New Yorkers. Classes are hosted at community organizations, schools, and shelters across the city. Volunteers will use the We Speak NYC curriculum which provides civic-focused multimedia resources created to empower adult immigrants through learning and practicing everyday English. The curriculum centers on an Emmy-Award winning educational drama series that informs learners about important New York City resources. The episodes address issues that most concern immigrants and asylum seekers such as health care, democracy, education, immigration legal help, elder care, and managing finances. Previous teaching experience is welcomed but not required! Tasks & responsibilities Attend and complete a 2-hour virtual training session, preparing you to lead conversation classes using our pedagogy and materials Complete a 1-hour sexual harassment prevention training once per year Be available to lead an in-person conversation class at a time and/or location you choose for 2 hours, once a week, for 8 weeks. *Please ensure you will be able to fully commit to the class schedule you chose for the entire duration of the cycle Engage with the WSNYC team throughout the duration of the cycle, including: participation in facilitator check-ins, class observation(s), short phone calls and completing a post-cycle survey How to apply Complete the volunteer interest form, linked here . As soon as the form is complete, you’ll start receiving information on upcoming trainings. WSNYC classes run in 4 cycles per year. The sooner you complete the volunteer interest form, the sooner you complete the training, the sooner you’ll be provided with specific cycle dates, locations, and times! Interested in or know a site that wants to host a class? Fill out our partner agreement application . Please reach out with any questions to: WeSpeakNYC@cityhall.nyc.gov

About the team 

Building on its Charter mandate, the Mayor’s Office of Immigrant Affairs (MOIA) promotes the well-being of immigrant communities by recommending policies and programs that facilitate the successful integration of immigrant New Yorkers into the civic, economic, and cultural life of the City. 

We Speak NYC is the city’s free English Language Learning program, created and managed by MOIA. We provide civic-focused instruction through videos, web and print materials, teacher professional development, and free community classes in all five boroughs. 

About the opportunity 

This program provides in-person English classes for new New Yorkers. Classes are hosted at community organizations, schools, and shelters across the city. 

Volunteers will use the We Speak NYC curriculum which provides civic-focused multimedia resources created to empower adult immigrants through learning and practicing everyday English.  

The curriculum centers on an Emmy-Award winning educational drama series that informs learners about important New York City resources. The episodes address issues that most concern immigrants and asylum seekers such as health care, democracy, education, immigration legal help, elder care, and managing finances.

Previous teaching experience is welcomed but not required! 

Tasks & responsibilities 

  • Attend and complete a 2-hour virtual training session, preparing you to lead conversation classes using our pedagogy and materials 

  • Complete a 1-hour sexual harassment prevention training once per year 

  • Be available to lead an in-person conversation class at a time and/or location you choose for 2 hours, once a week, for 8 weeks. *Please ensure you will be able to fully commit to the class schedule you chose for the entire duration of the cycle 

  • Engage with the WSNYC team throughout the duration of the cycle, including: participation in facilitator check-ins, class observation(s), short phone calls and completing a post-cycle survey 

How to apply 

Complete the volunteer interest form, linked here. As soon as the form is complete, you’ll start receiving information on upcoming trainings.  

WSNYC classes run in 4 cycles per year. The sooner you complete the volunteer interest form, the sooner you complete the training, the sooner you’ll be provided with specific cycle dates, locations, and times!

 

Interested in or know a site that wants to host a class? Fill out our partner agreement application.

Please reach out with any questions to: WeSpeakNYC@cityhall.nyc.gov

description: Bowery Residents’ Committee (BRC) is one of New York City’s largest and most comprehensive social service agencies, committed to supporting individuals who are experiencing homelessness or are at risk of becoming homeless. Each day, we see how deeply compassion can transform lives—and it is the generosity of volunteers like you that enables us to fulfill our mission with both heart and impact. The holiday season is our busiest time of year, and also one of the most meaningful. For many of the individuals we serve, Christmas can be a painful reminder of hardship and loss. Yet with the support of volunteers, it also becomes a moment of comfort, dignity, and genuine human connection. This year, BRC will host holiday celebrations at multiple locations across Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, and the Bronx on Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, and during the days leading up to the holiday. These gatherings bring warmth, joy, and a true sense of community to those we serve—and your participation would make an especially meaningful difference. Activities can include decorating and set-up of the service and dining areas, meal service, and post-meal clean up. If you’re interested in volunteering, please note that all volunteers must complete the BRC New Volunteer Registration Form (a link will be provided once you submit your interest here) and attend a brief orientation session . The sooner you complete these steps, the more opportunities will be available to you. Shifts are filled on a first-come, first-served basis and tend to reach capacity quickly, so early registration is encouraged. By planning ahead, you’ll have the best chance of securing a role that fits your schedule and allows you to make the greatest impact. Please note: Volunteers must be at least 18 years old to participate. We are not able to accommodate large groups at this time. Important: Please disregard any reference to specific locations, days, dates, or times that may appear in this posting. Each BRC program — located in Manhattan, Queens, the Bronx, and Brooklyn — will host its own holiday celebration on different days and times, both prior to and on the holiday itself. These shifts will be made available to those who have pre-registered once scheduling opens.

  • Bilingual volunteers are especially needed (Spanish, Korean, Mandarin, and others) 

Training: 

No previous tax experience is needed! You will receive hands-on training and ongoing support to prepare simple tax returns. Volunteers will be required to pass IRS volunteer certification exams to become IRS Certified VITA/TCE Volunteer Preparers.  

Time commitment: 

  • Minimum of one 4–8 hour shift per week (January–April 2026). 
  • Flexible scheduling: centers are open 7 days a week, including evenings and weekends. 
  • Extra shifts are welcome if your schedule allows. 

Why Volunteer? 

  • Empower hardworking New Yorkers to keep more of their money. 
  • Help families claim critical refunds and credits that can pay rent, buy food, and cover childcare needs. 
  • Gain skills in finance, problem-solving, and client service—great for résumés and careers. 
  • Join a diverse community of volunteers making a real impact in their city. 

👉 Take action today! Sign up now to become a NYC Free Tax Prep volunteer and help ensure every New Yorker gets the refund they deserve.
